'''Arts and culture'''
* [[Pope Francis]] opens the two-year [[Synod of Bishops in the Catholic Church|Ordinary General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops]]. This [[Synod on synodality|XVIth Synod of Bishops]], ends in Rome in October 2023. In his opening address, Pope Francis presented three “key words”: communion, participation, and mission. [https://www.catholicculture.org/news/headlines/index.cfm?storyid=52516 (Catholic World News)]

'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[2021 Niger attacks]]
***Ten people are killed and another is wounded as gunmen open fire at a [[mosque]] in the village of Abankor, [[Tillabéri]], [[Niger]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/villagers-killed-in-mosque-attack-in-western-niger/6269494.html (VOA)]
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Five soldiers are killed by rebels in a [[mountain pass]] in [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/11/kashmir-suspected-rebels-five-indian-soldiers (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**A spokesperson for the [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] says that the [[Ethiopian Ground Forces]] have launched a ground [[offensive (military)|offensive]] against rebels, with the support of local [[militia]]s of the [[Amhara Region]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ethiopian-army-starts-ground-offensive-against-rebellious-tigray-forces-regional-2021-10-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economist]]s [[David Card]], [[Joshua Angrist]] and [[Guido Imbens]] are awarded the 2021 [[Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences]] for their [[natural experiment]]s showing economic impacts. [https://www.dw.com/en/nobel-prize-in-economics-awarded-to-david-card-joshua-angrist-and-guido-imbens/a-59466055 (Deutsche Welle)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**The [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees]] reports that it has recovered the bodies of 15 people as well as 177 survivors from two Libyan [[coastguard]] boats returning to [[Libya]] after they attempted to cross the [[Mediterranean Sea]] in order to reach [[Europe]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/un-says-15-dead-attempted-migrant-voyage-libya-2021-10-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 China floods]]
**At least 15 people are killed and three are missing as heavy [[flood]]s affect [[Shanxi]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/12/several-killed-after-rains-batter-chinas-shanxi-province (Al Jazeera)]
*Two people are killed, and two homes and a [[United Parcel Service|UPS]] delivery van are destroyed after a [[Cessna 340]] crashes in [[Santee, California]], United States. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/11/us/san-diego-area-plane-crash/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
*****[[New South Wales]] (NSW) lifts [[COVID-19 lockdown|lockdown restrictions]] for [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|fully vaccinated]] residents after 107 days. Travel restrictions are lifted, businesses reopen in a limited capacity, and private and public gatherings are permitted with some restrictions. NSW residents who are not fully [[vaccinate]]d, with the exception of residents of some regional towns where infections are low, will be expected to continue to follow lockdown restrictions. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/oct/11/im-double-vaccinated-and-live-in-nsw-what-are-my-new-freedoms-today (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in New Zealand]]
****The [[New Zealand Government]] announces a new vaccine mandate that would require disability and [[healthcare workers]] to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 by December 1 and teachers by January 1, 2022, as the [[New Zealand|country]] suspends its "zero-COVID" strategy amid the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2021/10/11/new-zealand-mandates-covid-19-vaccines-for-health-workers-teachers-as-it-continues-to-battle-delta-outbreak/ (''Forbes'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea]]
****A two-week lockdown begins in [[Eastern Highlands Province]] as cases overwhelm hospitals and the number of deaths increases nationwide. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/453331/png-s-covid-crisis-swamps-highlands-hospitals (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wales]]
*****[[Wales]] begins to require people over the age of 18 to show their NHS COVID Pass or their proof of [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom|vaccination status]] in order to enter nightclubs, indoor non-seated events for more than 500 people, outdoor non-seated events for more than 4,000 people and any event with more than 10,000 people. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/uk/covid-pass-nightclubs-wales-rules-b959756.html (''Evening Standard'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] ends free [[COVID-19 testing]] for non-medical reasons in order to encourage people to get [[COVID-19 vaccination in Germany|vaccinated]]. Children younger than twelve and pregnant women are exempt from this rule. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/germany-ends-free-covid-19-tests-to-promote-vaccination/2388898# (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Malaysia]] lifts a ban on non-urgent interstate travel and resumes international travel where [[Malaysians]] travelling internationally are exempt from MyTravelPass as the country reaches a target to fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in Malaysia|vaccinate]] 90% of its adult population. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-10-10/malaysia-to-begin-interstate-travel-as-90-adults-fully-jabbed (Bloomberg News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Prime Minister of Thailand|Prime Minister]] [[Prayut Chan-o-cha]] announces that [[Thailand]] plans to end [[quarantine]] requirements for fully vaccinated travellers from at least 10 low-risk countries beginning on November 1. Additionally, the [[Government of Thailand|government]] will allow entertainment venues to reopen on December 1 and permit [[Alcohol (drug)|alcohol]] sales at establishments. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58838189 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
****[[Texas]] governor [[Greg Abbott]] signs an [[executive order]] prohibiting all entities in the state, including private companies, from enacting [[vaccine mandate]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/texas-governor-bars-all-vaccine-mandates-state-2021-10-11/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[World Health Organization|WHO]]'s [[Strategic Advisory Group of Experts]] recommends that [[immunocompromised]] people receive a third dose of the vaccine due to the risk of [[breakthrough infection]]s after standard immunization. The panel also recommends that people over the age of 60 receive an additional dose of the [[BBIBP-CorV|Sinopharm]] or [[Coronavac|Sinovac]] vaccine three months after their second dose, citing the performance of the vaccines in [[Latin America]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-who-vaccines/who-advises-additional-covid-shot-for-immunocompromised-people-idUSKBN2H11II (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[1987 Burkinabé coup d'état]]
**The trial for the 1987 [[assassination]] of former leader of [[Burkina Faso]] [[Thomas Sankara]], known as the "African [[Che Guevara]]", begins in [[Ouagadougou]] against 14 people, including former [[president of Burkina Faso|president]] [[Blaise Compaoré]], who will be tried ''[[Trial in absentia|in absentia]]''. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/11/burkina-faso-to-open-trial-on-1987-sankara-assassination (Al Jazeera)]
*Two teenagers are arrested in [[Batemans Bay]], [[NSW]], [[Australia]], for killing 14 [[kangaroo]]s two days ago. The animals were found slaughtered on two different roads. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-58880177 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Iraqi parliamentary election]]
**Preliminary results show that the [[Sadrist Movement]] of [[Shia Islam in Iraq|Shiite]] cleric [[Muqtada al-Sadr]] will retain its plurality in the [[Council of Representatives of Iraq|Council of Representatives]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/sadrists-claim-most-seats-in-iraq-parliament-after-vote/ (AFP via ''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Alar Karis]] is sworn in as the 6th [[President of Estonia]], succeeding [[Kersti Kaljulaid]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/10/12/alar-karis-sworn-in-as-estonia-s-new-president (Euronews)]
'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Boston]]
**[[2021 Boston Marathon]]
***The 125th [[Boston Marathon]], which was postponed from May 28, 2020 due to the COVID-19 [[pandemic]], takes place. The men's [[marathon]] is won by [[Benson Kipruto]] and the women's marathon is won by [[Diana Kipyogei]], both from [[Kenya]]. [https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/32380733/kenyans-benson-kipruto-diana-kipyogei-win-125th-pandemic-delayed-boston-marathon (ESPN)]
